summary: J. S. Pade was an Indologist. He held posts as a Research Officer at the University of Chicago (attested 1963) and at the Oriental Institute in Vadodara (attested 1966).

J. Thomas Rimer is a Japanologist who studied at Princeton University and Columbia University. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1985), the University of Maryland, College Park (~1985–1991), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1991–2010).
J.-M. Grandjean was a linguist who studied at the University of Lyon under Paul Regnaud.

Linguist and Indologist Jaan Puhvel studied at McGill, Harvard under Joshua Whatmough, Uppsala under Stig Wikander, and in France under Georges Dumézil. He also studied at and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.

Jabez Cornelius Whitley was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Queens' College (1855–1859) and served as a missionary for the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts from 1862.

Jack Goody worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. After studying at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946), he held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~1954 to 1984.

Jack Kornfield is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dartmouth, Saybrook, and under Wing-tsit Chan, Ajahn Chah, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. He co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Spirit Rock Meditation Center.
Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at McMaster University in 1999 and held a post at the University of Sudbury.
Indologist Jacob Antoon van Velze studied at Utrecht University from ~1921 to 1938, where he completed his Ph.D. under Willem Caland and Jan Gonda.

Jacob Ensink was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and F. D. K. Bosch, and served as Lecturer of Indology at the University of Groningen (1954–1962).

Jacob Fisher works in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2021–2025) and has held posts at Nalanda Monastery, Wadham College, Oxford, and Tergar Osel Ling Monastery (2024).

Jacob Grimm was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1806). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).
Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He has held academic posts at the College of William & Mary and the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob Neusner was a religious studies scholar who studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and JTSA. He held posts at UW–Milwaukee, Brandeis, University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~1994–2014).

Jacob P. Dalton is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Idaho, Michigan, and UC Davis. He has held positions at SOAS, the British Library, Yale, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Jacob Samuel Speyer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University. He served as professor at the University of Groningen (1888–1903) and Leiden University (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig. He was a professor at the University of Basel (1879–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).
Jacobus Arntz worked in Indology and philosophy. He taught philosophy, philology, and natural sciences at Kuilenburg Seminary (1843–1847, 1862–1865) and the Major Seminary of Roermond.
Jacobus Marinus van der Hoogt was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Amsterdam in 1929 under the supervision of Barend Faddegon.
